working.formula: 0.8 × breaker rating (the breaker is 125% of a continuous load)

working.name: Wire chosen
working.note: The fewest elements that work, then the thickest standard gauge (ASTM B258) for them: at or above the smallest diameter, with a coil that fits the groove at a pitch of 2–4 wire diameters. Thicker wire lasts longer (Kanthal).

working.formula: L = U²/P · (πd²/4) / ρ_T

working.formula: turns = L / (π·(D − d)); pitch = groove length / turns

working.name: Coil

working.formula: installed power ÷ inside area of the element walls

working.name: Installed power per unit of chamber volume
working.note: For comparison, 7 cu ft cone 10 kilns from L&L and Skutt have about 1650–1720 W/ft³ (electric-and-thermal.md §7 [S73, S74]).

working.formula: k = d/(r + d/2) ÷ η(90°) ≥ 2; H_min ≤ H_max, each the loads' moment about the touching point over its height to the crown's line; x_R = (N·x_p + G₁·e/2 + G₂·(d + e)/2 + G₃·(e − b_c/2) + H_min·h_s)/ΣV ≤ e; H_min/N ≤ μ
working.name: The door's arch and jambs
working.note: HarbisonWalker's arch method covers roof arches of T/S 4–10 %, and this door arch's ring is 12% of its span: so the statics here are Heyman's, from the geometry and the loads alone, which need no range. A jamb that gives a little lets the arch settle to its least thrust, so that is what it must hold (Heyman). A hot arch held rigidly would push towards the most; a door arch's hot thrust is not sourced (door-headers.md §D8). The whole wall over the arch is taken to bear on it, BIA's safe side. Sliding uses BIA's friction between brick masonry units, 0.6: for clay brick, none is sourced for insulating firebrick or refractory joints (refractory-bearing.md §B4.1). The left wall bonded into the jamb's end is counted for a length of the jamb wall's thickness only (a design rule, door-headers.md §D9). A partition wall bonded in between doors isn't counted.
working.reference: Heyman's safe theorem: masonry stands if a line of thrust in equilibrium with its loads lies within it, the line found need not be the actual one; domes-over-doors.md §D3, arch-thrust-theory.md §2; the minimum thrust, the line of thrust from the crown's extrados touching the intrados: 'an arch on spreading supports will act in a state of minimum thrust' (Heyman, The Stone Skeleton; arch-thrust-theory.md §2 [A1], [A3]), the least it pushes on its neighbours (domes-over-doors.md §D3 [D7]); the resultant in the base's middle third: no tension at the joint (domes-over-doors.md §D3 [D7]; door-headers.md §D3.2, BIA TN 31A); a statics criterion, not an allowable stress; Couplet–Heyman minimum thickness, Rizzi et al. 2010; domes-over-doors.md §D3 [D5]
working.value: a 3 in ring over 24 in, 2.1 times the thinnest that stands; its thrust 8 lb at least, 17 lb at most; on the 10.0 in jamb the resultant 6.1 in in from the door's edge (its middle third to 6.7 in); at the springing it needs friction 0.25 of 0.6

working.note: Olsen's Rule 1 is the low end of Ward's range at cone 10. He calls most gas kilns overpowered: a 36 ft³ IFB updraft on 10,000 BTU/ft³/hr fires in about 8 hours. Ward's high end gives about 6–7 hours. The table's column is chosen by the hot face and assumes its construction; a thinner or thicker wall is checked by the energy balance at the top temperature (gas.top), from this kiln's own heat loss.
working.reference: Ward Burner Systems Data Guide; combustion-and-masonry.md §3.1 [S28]; Olsen, The Kiln Book, 4th ed., p.226–228 (Rule 1)

working.formula: low end × volume
working.name: Design burner input

working.formula: 0.8 × min(20 psi, p_v − 20 psi)
working.name: Propane pressure available
working.note: The regulator needs its inlet 20 psi over its setting, and at full flow delivers 20 % under it; the burners' ratings go to 20 psi.
working.reference: NIST Chemistry WebBook, pure propane; combustion-and-masonry.md §1.2 [S6]; the liquid 20 °F under the air under draw; combustion-and-masonry.md §2.3 [S1], §2.8; RegO 597F series data sheet: capacity rated with the inlet 20 psig above the set pressure and delivery 20 % below it; combustion-and-masonry.md §2.8 [S89]

findings.message: Morgan Thermal Ceramics JM 26 insulating firebrick runs up to 2345 °F (data to 2012 °F); past its data sheet's points the conductivity is carried on along the nearest pair of points above the data, and held at the first point's value below it (no lower: more heat loss, the safe side).
findings.reference: electric-and-thermal.md §4.1, Morgan JM IFB series data sheet, 01 January 2025, BR.05

findings.message: Morgan Thermal Ceramics K-23 insulating firebrick runs down to 237.4 °F (data from 500 °F); past its data sheet's points the conductivity is carried on along the nearest pair of points above the data, and held at the first point's value below it (no lower: more heat loss, the safe side).
findings.reference: electric-and-thermal.md §4.1, Morgan K IFB series [S31]

findings.message: Arch bricks: Back wall, layer 1 from the inside, above the springline: about 4 bricks by volume, cut to the arch's curve; Back wall, layer 2 from the inside, above the springline: about 2 bricks by volume, cut to the arch's curve; Front wall, layer 1 from the inside, above the springline: about 4 bricks by volume, cut to the arch's curve; Front wall, layer 2 from the inside, above the springline: about 2 bricks by volume, cut to the arch's curve; Left wall, the skewback and fill on top: about 22 bricks by volume, cut to the arch's angle; Right wall, the skewback and fill on top: about 22 bricks by volume, cut to the arch's angle.
findings.reference: Arch and wedge shapes, 9-inch series; electric-and-thermal.md §5 [S54]

findings.message: The skewbacks and the fill beside the arch are drawn along the arch's radius at the springline and counted by volume. The skewback's face must match the arch: 60° to the horizontal here, 90° less half the arch's central angle (HarbisonWalker's 60° skews suit a 60° arch, its 48° skews one at 2.302 in/ft). The steel that takes the arch's thrust is in the frame.
findings.reference: kiln-hardware.md §5.2 [S20]

findings.message: HarbisonWalker, for industrial furnaces: "A stretcher course should never be used immediately below the skewback." Brick in these side walls is laid as stretchers, as in Olsen's insulating-brick kilns, whose featheredge skewbacks sit on a stretcher hot face (p.176, p.140). Where you can, lay the course under each skewback as headers.
findings.reference: kiln-hardware.md §4.1 [S20]; Olsen, The Kiln Book, 4th ed., p.176

findings.message: Castable: cure 16–24 h above 60 °F kept damp, never let it freeze, and dry it out slowly before the first firing (for Mizzou: 75 °F/h with a ½ h hold per inch at 250, 500 and 1000 °F). Follow the maker's sheet for your castable.
findings.reference: combustion-and-masonry.md §6.2 [S54, S56]

findings.message: Brick counts assume dry joints at the nominal 9 × 4½ × 2½ in size, a ⅛ in saw cut, and 5 % extra for breakage. Each cut piece already takes its own brick in the count. The size is sourced; the saw cut is an assumption no source gives, so adjust it to your saw. The allowance is the masonry estimators' "at least 5 percent" (BIA): set allowances.brick in the design from your own experience. At the corners the side walls run through and the back and door fit between them, layer by layer.
findings.reference: 9 × 4½ × 2½ in straight; electric-and-thermal.md §5 [S54]; kerf assumed; brick-waste.md §1, BIA Technical Note 10 (2009), p.11 [W1]
